description: Maintain users' tasks with sequential global IDs, due dates, descriptions, tags, and completion state. Queries return only pending descriptions in due-date order, optionally filtered by a tag. Example 1: a user's tasks due on days 4 and 2 are returned in the order of day 2 then day 4. Example 2: completing a task removes it from both task queries, but does not affect another user's task. Constraints: IDs are sequential, due dates are unique, and completion applies only to a task owned by that user.
intuition: Each user's active task records can be filtered and sorted by the unique due date.

brute_force.approach: Keep all records in one list and scan every task for each user's query.
brute_force.time: addTask O(1), completeTask O(n), query O(n log n)

optimal.approach: Map each user to task records and use a global increasing task ID; sort only that user's matching active tasks for a query.
optimal.time: addTask O(1), completeTask O(1) expected, query O(t log t)

edge_cases: Completing a missing task or another user's task has no effect.
Completed tasks never appear in tag-filtered or unfiltered results.
